{"content":"# Proof Obligations for `double-distributes-over-add`

Target theorem (from `formalization.md`):

    Forall a : Int. Forall b : Int.
      Eq( add(double(a), double(b)), double(add(a, b)) )

Decomposed into two tiers. **Tier A** obligations are discharged mechanically —
the kernel (`kernel.py`) re-checks each one against the explicit proof steps in
`formalization.md` §6. **Tier B** obligations are meta-level (trusted-base)
checks discharged by review and by a model sanity check.

A step is *discharged* only when the kernel accepts it; nothing is trusted from
the proof text itself.

---

## Tier A — kernel-discharged obligations

### O0. Static well-formedness (run once on the input file)

- [ ] **O0.1 Sort correctness.** Every application `add(M, N)` has both
  arguments of sort `Int`; every application `double(M)` has `M : Int`; all
  variables (`a, b, n, x, y, z`) have sort `Int`. No ill-sorted term occurs in
  any axiom, theorem, proof step, or substitution.
- [ ] **O0.2 Closed axioms.** The bodies of `double-def`, `add-assoc`,
  `add-comm` contain no free variables (each variable is bound by its `Forall`).
- [ ] **O0.3 Theorem–proof match.** The declared theorem formula is closed and
  syntactically identical to the final proof step `main-2`.
- [ ] **O0.4 Justification references.** Every `(cong/sym/trans/gen)` reference
  points to an *earlier* step; no cycles, no dangling names.

### O1. Definitional unfolding — axiom instances of `double-def` (D1)

- [ ] **O1.1 (step `e1`)** `Eq(double(a), add(a,a))` is D1's body under
  capture-avoiding substitution `{n := a}`.
- [ ] **O1.2 (step `e2`)** `Eq(double(b), add(b,b))` is D1's body under
  `{n := b}`.
- [ ] **O1.3 (step `e3`)** `Eq(double(add(a,b)), add(add(a,b), add(a,b)))` is
  D1's body under `{n := add(a,b)}`.

*Acceptance:* kernel matches each formula against the instantiated axiom body
exactly (no up-to-conversion).

### O2. Interchange chain — the mathematical core

Subgoal **G2**: `Eq( add(add(a,a), add(b,b)), add(add(a,b), add(a,b)) )`
(the instance `x:=a, y:=a, z:=b, w:=b` of the interchange law
`(x+y)+(z+w) = (x+z)+(y+w)`; proven inline rather than as a general lemma).

Let `T0 = add(add(a,a), add(b,b))` and `T10 = add(add(a,b), add(a,b))`.
Each step below must be accepted as either a whole-term `AXIOM` instance
(context `_`) or a `CONG` application whose context contains exactly one `_`:

- [ ] **O2.1 (c1)**  `T0 = T1`  — A1 `{x:=a, y:=a, z:=add(b,b)}`, context `_`
- [ ] **O2.2 (c2)**  `T1 = T2`  — A1 `{x:=a, y:=b, z:=b}`, context `add(a, _)`
- [ ] **O2.3 (c3)**  `T2 = T3`  — A2 `{x:=a, y:=b}`, context `add(a, add(_, b))`
- [ ] **O2.4 (c4)**  `T3 = T4`  — A1 `{x:=b, y:=a, z:=b}`, context `add(a, _)`
- [ ] **O2.5 (c5)**  `T4 = T5`  — A2 `{x:=a, y:=b}`, context `add(a, add(b, _))`
- [ ] **O2.6 (c6)**  `T5 = T6`  — A1 `{x:=b, y:=b, z:=a}`, context `add(a, _)`
- [ ] **O2.7 (c7)**  `T6 = T7`  — A1 `{x:=a, y:=add(b,b), z:=a}`, context `_`
- [ ] **O2.8 (c8)**  `T7 = T8`  — A1 `{x:=a, y:=b, z:=b}`, context `add(_, a)`
- [ ] **O2.9 (c9)**  `T8 = T9`  — A1 `{x:=add(a,b), y:=b, z:=a}`, context `_`
- [ ] **O2.10 (c10)** `T9 = T10` — A2 `{x:=b, y:=a}`, context `add(add(a,b), _)`
- [ ] **O2.11 (chain)** `Eq(T0, T10)` follows by nested `TRANS` over
  `c1 … c10`; the kernel must check that each adjacent pair shares its middle
  term (`T1, T2, …, T9` match syntactically).

### O3. Definitional unfolding of the goal's two sides

- [ ] **O3.1 (lhs)** `Eq( add(double(a), double(b)), T0 )` — two `CONG` steps
  and one `TRANS`:
  - O3.1a: `CONG` of `e1` in context `add(_, double(b))`;
  - O3.1b: `CONG` of `e2` in context `add(add(a,a), _)`;
  - O3.1c: `TRANS` of the two, with matching middle term
    `add(add(a,a), double(b))`.
- [ ] **O3.2 (rhs)** `Eq( T10, double(add(a,b)) )` — `SYM` of `e3`.

### O4. Assembly and quantification

- [ ] **O4.1 (main-raw)** `Eq( add(double(a), double(b)), double(add(a,b)) )`
  by `TRANS lhs (TRANS chain rhs)`; kernel checks both middle-term matches.
- [ ] **O4.2 (main-1)** `GEN a` over `main-raw`. *Side condition:* `a` is not
  free in any open hypothesis. The system has no hypotheses (every step chains
  back to closed axioms), so the condition holds; the kernel must confirm the
  justification DAG of `main-raw` contains only closed-axiom-derived steps.
- [ ] **O4.3 (main-2)** `GEN b` over `main-1`; same side condition; result must
  be identical to the declared theorem (also O0.3).

**Dependency graph (must be acyclic, enforced by O0.4):**

```
e1, e2 ──► lhs ─┐
c1…c10 ─► chain ┼─► main-raw ─► main-1 (GEN a) ─► main-2 (GEN b)
e3 ─────► rhs ──┘
```

## Tier B — trusted-base obligations (meta-level)

- [ ] **O5.1 Rule soundness review.** Each of the six kernel rules
  (`AXIOM, REFL, SYM, TRANS, CONG, GEN`) is semantically sound in every FOL=
  structure: an instance of a valid axiom is valid; REFL/SYM/TRANS/CONG
  preserve truth under any assignment; GEN preserves truth when the variable is
  not free in open hypotheses (none exist). Reviewed once per kernel change.
- [ ] **O5.2 Kernel correctness review.** The implementation of the rule
  checker (substitution is capture-avoiding; `CONG` contexts have exactly one
  hole; `TRANS` middle terms are matched syntactically) is reviewed and covered
  by negative tests (rejected malformed steps).
- [ ] **O5.3 Non-vacuity / model check.** ℤ with `add ↦ +`, `double ↦ n ↦ 2n`
  satisfies `T`: spot-verify `add-assoc`, `add-comm`, `double-def` on sample
  integers. This upgrades “`T ⊢ φ`” to “φ is true of the integers”.

---

## Status summary

| Tier | Obligations | Count | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | O0 | 4 | pending — discharged by kernel run |
| A | O1 | 3 | pending — discharged by kernel run |
| A | O2 | 11 | pending — discharged by kernel run |
| A | O3 | 2 | pending — discharged by kernel run |
| A | O4 | 3 | pending — discharged by kernel run |
| B | O5 | 3 | pending — review + spot check |

All 26 obligations must be discharged before the informal claim in `claim.md`
counts as formally verified. O2.1–O2.10 and O1 carry the only mathematical
content; the remainder are structural bookkeeping enforced by the kernel.
